name: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms (MTR)
why_it_matters: Founded in 1924 by the Maiya brothers from Parampalli, MTR invented rava idli during WWII rice shortages and remains the city's most cited Udupi institution. The Lalbagh Road original is also one of only ~150 entries on the World's Legendary Restaurants list.
insider_tip: Take a token from the counter on entry, then wait upstairs for table service; the lunch thali (1 to 3 pm) is unlimited and the better-value meal vs. a dosa rush. Closed Mondays.

name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
why_it_matters: Started in 1943 as a tiny eatery for students of nearby colleges, Vidyarthi Bhavan's slow-cooked, ghee-soaked masala dosa is the benchmark Bengaluru measures all others against. The narrow Gandhi Bazaar shopfront and shared-table format have not changed in eight decades.
insider_tip: Arrive between 7 and 9 am on a weekday; the queue snakes around the lane after 10 am and wait times can hit 45 minutes. Closed Mondays. Cash and UPI only.
signature_address: 32, Gandhi Bazaar Main Road, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: CTR Shri Sagar (Central Tiffin Room)
why_it_matters: Established in 1920 by Y.V. Subramanyam, CTR is the city's reference point for benne (butter) masala dosa — crisp outer, soft inner, served with a thick coconut chutney. Now formally called Shri Sagar but locals still queue for what they grew up calling CTR.
insider_tip: The kitchen shuts between 12.30 pm and 4 pm — plan a breakfast or evening visit, not lunch. Pair the benne dosa with khara bath rather than a second dosa for the fuller flavour spread.
signature_address: 152, 7th Cross Road, Margosa Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
why_it_matters: Opened in 1965 by K.V. Nagesh Rao and K.N. Saraswati, Brahmin's serves only four things — idli, vada, khara bath, kesari bath — and is regularly named the city's best plate of soft idli with watery, mint-tinted coconut chutney. The same family runs it three generations on.
insider_tip: Stand-and-eat only, no chairs. Get there before 8.30 am to skip the office queue, and ask for the chutney refill — they pour generously if you don't waste the first cup. Closed Sundays.
signature_address: Ranga Rao Road, Near Shankar Mutt, Shankarapuram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Veena Stores
why_it_matters: A standing-only counter on 15th Cross since 1977, Veena Stores is the place locals send first-timers when they want to argue that Malleshwaram has the city's softest idli. The chutney spread (coconut, mint, peanut) is unusually generous for a street counter.
insider_tip: Open all seven days, 7 am to noon and 4 pm onwards. Ask for an extra chutney pour at the counter — they'll oblige if you don't push. UPI works; carry small notes for the tip.
signature_address: 187, 15th Cross, Margosa Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

name: Hotel Janatha
why_it_matters: A 1965 darshini on the same Sajjan Rao Circle stretch as the VV Puram food street, Janatha is one of two Basavanagudi names tied to the khali dosa — a soft, plain dosa eaten with coconut chutney. Workhorse menu, low prices, full at 8 am sharp.
insider_tip: Two sittings only — 6.30 am to noon and 3 pm to 7 pm. Order khali dosa with extra chutney; the masala version is solid but the plain one is what people return for.
signature_address: 26, Diagonal Road, Sajjan Rao Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: New Modern Hotel
why_it_matters: Opened 1959 near Minerva Circle, NMH was a gathering room for Kannada writers (DVG, H.V. Seetharamaiah) and theatre figures (Girish Kasaravalli) — its masala dosa and rich badam halwa are both Basavanagudi reference dishes. Lodging-and-boarding format from a different era.
insider_tip: Be in by 9 am to avoid the office rush. Order the masala dosa with a side of badam halwa — sweet first or last is a long-running local debate worth settling for yourself.
signature_address: 143, Dr. A.N. Krishna Rao Road, Near Minerva Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Hotel Dwaraka
why_it_matters: Started 1972 on Bull Temple Road and now in NR Colony, Hotel Dwaraka is widely credited as the originator of Bengaluru's kali dosa — a soft, oil-less dosa cooked on a closed pan that arrived to the city before any other restaurant put it on a menu. Cash-only, self-service.
insider_tip: Cash only, no card or wallet. Avarekalu khara bath is seasonal (Dec to Feb when local field beans are in) — ask before ordering, it's the better khara bath outside the season.
signature_address: 7th Cross, NR Colony, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Halli Mane
why_it_matters: Halli Mane (Kannada for 'village home') is the city's most cited address for rural Karnataka vegetarian cooking — ragi mudde, akki rotti, jolada rotti, bisi bele bath, obbattu — served on banana leaves in a low-seating, village-themed room. Operating on Sampige Road for 20+ years.
insider_tip: The unlimited weekend breakfast buffet is the best value way to taste eight to ten Karnataka village dishes in one sitting. Ask the server which obbattu (holige) filling is freshest that day — coconut, dal or jaggery.
signature_address: 14, 3rd Cross, Sampige Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

name: Vasudev Adiga's
why_it_matters: K.N. Vasudev Adiga, son of Brahmin's Coffee Bar founder K.V. Nageshwar Adiga, opened the first Adiga's on DVG Road in 1993 as a clean, low-priced darshini. The chain is now the city's reference quality bar for what a darshini should taste like — same recipes across 12+ Bengaluru outlets.
insider_tip: The Jayanagar 4th Block branch runs a faster turnaround than the AC restaurants — pay first at the counter, then collect from the kitchen window. Best for a 15-minute weekday breakfast stop.
